BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to creating the Washington health partnership;adding new sections to chapter 41.05 RCW; adding a new section tochapter 74.09 RCW; adding a new section to chapter 43.370 RCW; addinga new section to chapter 74.38 RCW; adding a new section to chapter48.02 RCW; and adding a new chapter to Title 82 RCW.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BillSection.RCWSLText: The legislature finds that: (1) Nationally and locally health care costs are inflating fasterthan the consumer price index and wages; (2) Since 1980, health care costs have increased from nine percentto sixteen percent of the nation's gross domestic product, and areexpected to exceed twenty percent by 2016; (3) Other industrialized nations provide universal health carecoverage, but spend much less. Some spend less than half as much perperson; (4) In 2007, the average annual premium for family coverage wasmore than twelve thousand dollars, of which over three thousand dollarsare paid by the worker; p. 1 SB 6221 (5) In 2008, of Washingtonians under the age of sixtyfive, overone million three hundred thousand will spend more than ten percent oftheir pretax family income on health care costs. Eightyfour of thesepeople have insurance; (6) Every thirty seconds, someone in this country files forbankruptcy in the aftermath of a serious health problem. Of those whofile for bankruptcy, sixtyeight percent had health insurance; (7) In Washington state, approximately thirty cents of every dollarreceived by hospitals and doctors' offices is consumed by theadministrative expenses of the health plans and the providers. Beforethe doctors and hospitals receive the funds for delivering the care,approximately fourteen percent of the insurance premium has alreadybeen consumed by health plan administration; (8) In 2006, hospitals, physicians, community clinics, and otherproviders spent a combined total of five hundred eightyfour milliondollars in uncompensated care for the uninsured, a twentyeight percentincrease since 2002; (9) The institute of medicine estimates that between thirty andforty cents associated with every health care dollar is spent on costsof poor quality - overuse, underuse, misuse, duplication, systemfailures, unnecessary repetition, poor communication, and adverseevents attributable to medical errors; (10) Rising costs have led to a decline in employerprovided healthbenefits. In Washington, since 1993, employerbased coverage declinedfrom seventyone percent to sixtyfive percent; (11) In 2007, fewer than half of small employers in Washington areable to offer coverage to their employees; (12) Rising costs are seriously threatening the physical and fiscalwellbeing of Washingtonians, the ability of Washington businesses tocompete globally, farms to thrive, government to provide neededservices, schools to educate, and local citizens to form new andsuccessful business ventures.

(1) The Washington health partnership isestablished as a public-private entity to provide comprehensive healthcoverage to all residents of the state of Washington. (2) In establishing and administering the health care system, theWashington health partnership shall seek to attain the following goals: SB 6221 p. 2 (a) By 2012, every resident of this state shall have access toaffordable, comprehensive health care services; (b) Services shall be provided through the private health caresector; (c) The plan shall maintain and improve choice of health careproviders and high quality health care services in this state; and (d) The plan shall include costcontainment strategies that retainand assure affordable coverage for all Washingtonians.

The definitions in this section applythroughout this chapter unless the context clearly requires otherwise. (1) "Board" means the board of trustees of the partnership. (2) "Eligible person" means a person who meets the eligibilityrequirements of section 8 of this act. (3) "Enrollee" means an eligible person who is enrolled in apartnership plan. (4) "Medical home" means a health care provider who providesprimary care for the enrollee and who is identified as the keyprofessional responsible for coordinating all medical care for a givenenrollee, including referral to a specialist. "Medical home" includesgeneral practice physicians, family practitioners, internists,pediatricians, obstetricians and gynecologists, advanced practicenurses, certified nurse midwives, and physician assistants. "Medicalhome" may also include a specialist who is treating a person with achronic medical condition, disability, or special health care needs forwhich regular treatment by a specialist is medically necessary. (5) "Medical inflation" means changes in the consumer price indexfor all consumers, United States city average, for the medical caregroup, including medical care commodities and medical care services, asdetermined by the United States department of labor. (6) "Network" means: (a) A carrier as defined under RCW 48.41.030; or (b) A coordinated group of health care providers that is regulatedunder Title 48 RCW and is comprised of primary care physicians, medicalspecialists, physician assistants, nurses, clinics, one or morehospitals, and other health care providers and facilities, includingproviders and facilities that specialize in mental health services andalcohol or other drug abuse treatment. p. 3 SB 6221 (7) "Partnership" means the Washington health partnership, thepublic-private program sponsored and administered by the board. (8) "Plan" means a "health plan" as defined under chapter 48.41 RCWthat is offered by the Washington health partnership. (9) "Public employee" means an individual who retired or whoterminated employment due to disability from any of the entitiesdescribed in (a) through (d) of this subsection, and who is noteligible for parts A and B of medicare; or an individual employed by: (a) The state of Washington; (b) A school district or educational service district; (c) A public institution of higher education; or (d) A political subdivision of the state.

(1) The Washington health partnership isgoverned by a board composed of members nominated by the governor, withthe advice and consent of the senate, and appointed for staggered sixyear terms as follows: (a) The administrator of the health care authority who shall serveas the initial chairperson of the board until such time as the boardelects a chairperson; (b) Two members selected from a list of names submitted bystatewide labor or union coalitions, one of whom must be a publicemployee who is a union member; (c) Two members selected from a list of names submitted bystatewide business and employer organizations, one of whom must be apublic employer; (d) One member selected from a list of names submitted by statewidepublic school teacher labor organizations; (e) One member selected from a list of names submitted by statewidesmall business organizations; (f) One member who is a selfemployed person; (g) Two members selected from a list of names submitted bystatewide health care consumer organizations; and (h) Four members with experience in health benefit management andcost containment. (2) The terms of all members of the board expire on July 1st. Eachmember of the board holds office until a successor is appointed and SB 6221 p. 4 qualified unless the member vacates or is removed from his or heroffice. (a) A member who serves as a result of holding another office orposition vacates his or her office as a member when he or she vacatesthe other office or position. (b) A vacancy on the board must be filled in the same manner as theoriginal appointment to the board for the remainder of the unexpiredterm, if any. (c) A majority of the members of the board constitutes a quorum forthe purpose of conducting its business and exercising its powers andfor all other purposes, notwithstanding the existence of any vacancies.Action may be taken by the board upon a vote of a majority of themembers present. (d) Members of the board shall be compensated in accordance withRCW 43.03.250 and shall be reimbursed for their travel expenses whileon official business in accordance with RCW 43.03.050 and 43.03.060. (e) The board and employees of the board shall not be civilly orcriminally liable and shall not have any penalty or cause of action ofany nature arise against them for any action taken or not taken,including any discretionary decision or failure to make a discretionarydecision, when the action or inaction is done in good faith and in theperformance of the powers and duties under this chapter. Nothing inthis section prohibits legal actions against the board to enforce theboard's statutory or contractual duties or obligations.

The board shall: (1) Establish, fund, and manage the partnership as provided in thischapter; (2) Establish and appoint a technical advisory committee and mayseek the advice of technical experts when necessary to execute thepowers and duties included in this section; (3) Have discretion to delegate any powers and duties the boardconsiders proper to one or more of its members or its executivedirector; (4) Provide for mechanisms to enroll every eligible resident in thestate. Contracts entered into by the board with providers and brokersmust include provisions to enroll all eligible persons at the point of p. 5 SB 6221service, and outreach programs to assure every eligible person becomesenrolled in the plan; (5) Consistent with Title 48 RCW and in coordination with theinsurance commissioner, establish a patient bill of rights thatincludes a program for consumer protection and a process to resolvedisputes with networks or providers; (6) Establish an independent and binding appeals process forresolving disputes over eligibility and other determinations made bythe board. Any person who is adversely affected by a board eligibilitydetermination or any other determination is entitled to review of thedetermination; (7) Submit an annual report on its activities to the governor andeach chamber of the legislature; (8) Contract for annual, independent program evaluations andfinancial audits that measure the extent to which the plan is achievingthe goals under section 1 of this act. The board may not enter into acontract with the same auditor for more than five years; (9) Accept bids from networks in accordance with the criteria setout in section 13 of this act or make payments to feeforserviceproviders in accordance with this act. The board shall consult withthe health care authority in determining the most effective andefficient way to purchase health care benefits; and (10) Monitor networks and providers to assure their services meetthe plan objectives and criteria under this chapter.

The board shall have all the powersnecessary or convenient to carry out the purposes and provisions ofthis chapter. In addition to all other powers granted the board underthis chapter, the board may: (1) Adopt, amend, and repeal bylaws and policies and proceduresfor the regulation of its affairs and the conduct of its business; (2) Maintain an office; (3) Sue and be sued; (4) Accept gifts, grants, loans, or other contributions fromprivate or public sources; (5) Monitor the fiscal management of the partnership; (6) Execute contracts and other instruments, including contractsfor any professional services required for the authority; SB 6221 p. 6 (7) Employ any officers, agents, and employees that it may requireand determine their qualifications and compensation; (8) Procure liability insurance; (9) Contract for studies on issues, as identified by the board; (10) Borrow money, as necessary on a shortterm basis, to addresscash flow issues; and (11) Compel witnesses to attend meetings and to testify upon anynecessary matter concerning the plan.

For the purpose of establishing thepartnership, the board shall define all of the following terms: (1) "Place of permanent residence"; (2) "Substantial presence in this state." In defining "substantialpresence in this state," the board shall consider such factors as theamount of time per year that a person is actually present in the stateand the amount of taxes that a person pays in this state, except that: (a) If the person attends school outside of this state and is undertwentyfour years of age, the factors shall include the amount of timethat the person's parent or guardian is actually present in the stateand the amount of taxes that the person's parent or guardian pays inthis state; and (b) If the person is in active service with the United States armedforces outside of this state, the factors shall include the amount oftime that the person's parent, guardian, or spouse is actually presentin the state and the amount of taxes that the person's parent,guardian, or spouse pays in this state. (3) "Immediate family"; and (4) "Gainfully employed." The definition must include employmentby persons who are selfemployed and persons who work on farms.

(1) A person and the members of the person'simmediate family are eligible to participate in the partnership if theperson satisfies all of the following criteria: (a) The person has maintained his or her place of permanentresidence, as defined by the board, in this state for at least twelvemonths; (b) The person maintains a substantial presence in this state, asdefined by the board; and p. 7 SB 6221 (c) The person is not: (i) Eligible for health care coverage from a foreign government orthe federal government, including medicare and medicaid; (ii) An inmate of a state correctional institution, as defined inRCW 9.94.049; or (iii) Placed or confined in, or committed to, an institution forthe mentally ill or developmentally disabled as described in 42 U.S.C.Sec. 1396 et seq. (2) A child under age eighteen who resides in this state with hisor her parent is eligible to participate in the plan regardless of thelength of time the child has resided in this state, and regardless ofwhether the parent met the residency requirements, subject torequirements outlined in subsection (1)(c)(i) of this section. (3) A pregnant woman who resides in this state who does not yetmeet the residency requirements is eligible to participate in the planregardless of the length of time the pregnant woman has resided in thisstate, subject to requirements outlined in subsection (1)(c)(i) of thissection. (4) Public employees as defined in section 3 of this act, and byrules established by the board, shall receive health coverage under thepartnership, effective January 1, 2010. (5) A person who is eligible to participate in the partnershipunder subsection (1), (2), or (4) of this section and who receiveshealth care coverage under a collective bargaining agreement that is ineffect on January 1, 2010, is eligible to participate in thepartnership on the day on which the collective bargaining agreementexpires or the day after the collective bargaining agreement isextended, modified, or renewed to reflect the intention of groupparticipation in the partnership.

The partnership shall implement outreach andeducation efforts to facilitate informed enrollment. (1) The partnership may contract with insurance brokers,associations, local government, and notforprofit organizations toperform the outreach and educational functions specified in thissection. (2) The partnership shall: SB 6221 p. 8 (a) Employ various methods and media to communicate information tothe public about the partnership; (b) Actively engage in outreach to eligible individuals and assisteligible persons to enroll in their choice of health care coverageunder the partnership; (c) Assist eligible persons in choosing health care coverage byproviding cost, quality, and geographic coverage information regardingchoice of available networks and providers; (d) Assist eligible persons to select a medical home; (e) Inform plan enrollees of the role they can play in holding downhealth care costs by taking advantage of preventive care, enrolling inchronic disease management programs if appropriate, responsibly usingmedical services such as emergency rooms and specialists, and engagingin healthy lifestyles. The partnership shall inform enrollees ofnetworks or workplaces which provide healthy lifestyle incentives; (f) Consistent with Title 48 RCW and in coordination with theinsurance commissioner and the board, establish a process for resolvingdisputes with providers; (g) Act as an advocate for plan enrollees having questions,difficulties, or complaints about their health care services orcoverage, including investigating and attempting to resolve thecomplaint; (h) If an enrollee's complaint cannot be successfully resolved,inform the enrollee of any legal or other means of recourse for his orher complaint, consistent with the patient bill of rights in section 5of this act. If the complaint involves a dispute over covered benefitsor services provided, the enrollee must be directed to the appealsprocess established under Title 48 RCW. If the complaint involves adispute over eligibility or other determinations made by the board, theenrollee must be directed to the appeals process for board decisions;and (i) Provide information to the public, agencies, legislators, andothers regarding problems and concerns of plan enrollees and makerecommendations for resolving those problems and concerns. (3) The partnership and its employees and contractors shall nothave any conflict of interest relating to the performance of theirduties. When a conflict of interest is discovered, the office shall p. 9 SB 6221modify or terminate its relationship with that entity to remove theconflict of interest.

(1) The partnership shall establish ahealth care program that will take effect on January 1, 2010. Theprogram shall provide a standardized set of covered services, subjectto limitations as determined by the board and consistent with the costsharing requirements in section 11 of this act, including: (a) Air and ground ambulance services; (b) Diabetic education; (c) Diagnostic testing; (d) Durable medical equipment, supplies, and prostheses; (e) Emergency room; (f) Hearing examination and hardware; (g) Home health care; (h) Hospital services, including: (i) Inpatient facility services; (ii) Inpatient professional services; (iii) Outpatient surgery facility services; and (iv) Outpatient surgery professional services; (i) Inpatient and outpatient chemical dependency services; (j) Inpatient and outpatient mental health care; (k) Integrated longterm health coverage, including home health,hospice, and skilled nursing care; (l) Neurodevelopmental therapy for children ages six and younger; (m) Obstetric and well newborn care; (n) Office and clinic visits; (o) Organ transplants; (p) Physical, occupational, speech, and massage therapies; (q) Prescription drugs, insulin, and disposable diabetic supplies; (r) Preventive care; (s) Radiation and chemotherapy services; (t) Skilled nursing; (u) Spinal manipulations; (v) Temporomandibular joint (TMJ) disorder treatment; and (w) Vision exams and hardware. (2) The board: SB 6221 p. 10 (a) May adjust the covered services or payment methods to provideadditional or different treatment options if they are cost-effectiveand there is scientific evidence that the options are likely to reducehealth care costs, avoid health risks, or result in better healthoutcomes; (b) May offer enrollees incentives that promote healthy life stylesor compliance with evidence-based treatment; (c) Shall review recommendations from the health technologyclinical committee, as described under RCW 70.14.090, and modifybenefits to reflect the recommendations of that committee; (d) Shall review research on evidencebased best practices and takesteps to promote such practices in the partnership, including: (i) Educating networks and providers on evidencebased bestpractices; (ii) Sharing data with networks and providers on the extent towhich they follow evidencebased best practices; and (iii) Providing incentives or disincentives, when appropriate, topromote use of evidencebased best practices; and (e) Consistent with chapter 19.68 RCW, shall establish regulationsto restrict or prohibit arrangements where a health provider, or familymember, would financially benefit by the health provider referringpatients to a specific health service. Such financial arrangementsinclude, but are not limited to, referrals to diagnostic imagingservices, pathology services, or ambulatory surgical services where thereferring health provider has a financial interest. (3) If cost-effective, the board may establish or contract for atoll-free hotline that is available twenty-four hours a day, seven daysa week, staffed by persons qualified to advise enrollees on health careissues. (4) A union may bargain or an employer may pay for: (a) Benefits not covered by subsection (1) of this section; and (b) Some or all employee cost-sharing charges.

(1) The following evidencebased, coveredservices are not subject to any pointofservice costsharingrequirement: (a) Prenatal care for pregnant women; (b) Well baby care; p. 11 SB 6221 (c) Well child examinations and immunizations for children up toeighteen years of age; (d) Other preventive services or procedures, as determined by theboard, for which there is scientific evidence that exemption from costsharing is likely to reduce health care costs or avoid health risks;and (e) Chronic care services, provided that the enrollee receiving theservices is participating in, and complying with, a chronic diseasemanagement program, as defined by the board. (2)(a) The board shall set maximum deductible amounts for eachcalendar year enrollment period, and shall consider separatedeductibles for: (i) An enrollee who is eighteen years of age or older on January1st of that year; and (ii) A family consisting of two or more enrollees who are eighteenyears of age or older on January 1st of that year. (b) The board shall determine whether an enrollee who is undereighteen years of age on January 1st of that year must pay anydeductible. (c) The board shall establish rules to assure that deductibles donot pose a barrier to enrollees receiving medically necessary services. (3) The board shall establish, and update, not more often thanannually, a system of copayments and/or coinsurance that will promoteappropriate use of health care services, but not pose a barrier toenrollees receiving appropriate care. At a minimum, the board shallset copayments that promote: (a) Appropriate emergency room use; (b) Appropriate use of specialists; (c) Evidencebased, costeffective use of prescription drugs basedon presence on the formulary or generic status of a drug, except thatall enrollees, regardless of age, shall pay no more for a prescriptiondrug than the actual cost of the prescription drug plus the negotiateddispensing fee. (4) The board shall establish a maximum amount for costsharing,including deductibles, copayments and coinsurance that an individual ora family shall pay in a calendar year enrollment period. Inestablishing maximum amounts, the board shall consider mechanisms to SB 6221 p. 12 reduce cost-sharing for individuals below two hundred percent of thefederal poverty level. (5) The board shall establish a premiumsharing schedule for allpartnership enrollees. In designing the premiumsharing schedule, theboard shall charge enrollees in a benchmark plan a zero premium. Theboard shall establish higher premiums for highercost networks and maycharge an enrollee in a highercost network a monthly premium equal tothe full price bid by that network less the full price bid by thelowestcost network.

(1) The board may establish areas in thestate, which may be single counties, multicounty regions, or otherareas, for the purpose of receiving bids from networks. These areasshall be established to maximize the level and quality of competitionor to increase the number of provider choices available to eligiblepersons and enrollees in the areas. (2) In each area designated by the board under subsection (1) ofthis section, the board shall offer one or more network options, ifavailable. Each network must be certified and meet the qualifyingcriteria in section 13 of this act. (3) The board shall also offer a "fee-for-service option" acrossthe state. The board shall: (a) Establish feeforservice payment rates for all health careservices and articles covered under the plan; (b) Contract with one or more plan administrators selected througha competitive procurement process to administer the feeforserviceoption; (c) Ensure that the fee-for-service option meets the requirementsof section 13(2) (b) through (f) of this act; (d) Ensure that enrollees selecting the feeforservice optionchoose a medical home.

(1) The partnership shall annually solicitsealed premium bids from competing networks for the purpose of offeringhealth care coverage to enrollees in the Washington health partnership.After three full years of operation, the partnership may solicit bidsno less frequently than every three years. p. 13 SB 6221 (2) A network is a qualifying network if it demonstrates to thesatisfaction of the board that: (a) The fixed monthly riskadjusted amount that it bids reasonablyreflects its estimated actual costs for providing enrollees with suchbenefits, except that the network may not artificially underbid for thepurpose of gaining market share; (b) It spends at least eighty-eight percent of the revenue itreceives under this chapter on: (i) Payments to health care providers to provide the health carebenefits specified in this act to enrollees who choose the network; or (ii) Investments, such as capital improvements, that the networkcan reasonably demonstrate to the board will improve the overallquality or lower the overall cost of patient care; (c) It meets standards of access, as determined by the board incoordination with the office of the insurance commissioner under Title48 RCW, that assure enrollees can gain reasonable access to servicesfrom physicians, physician assistants, nurses, clinics, hospitals, andother health care providers and facilities, including providers andfacilities that specialize in mental health services and alcohol orother drug abuse treatment; (d) It provides each enrollee with medically appropriate and highquality health care services as established in section 10 of this actor as modified by the board, in a highly coordinated manner, including: (i) Appropriate use of primary care, medical specialists,medications, and hospital emergency rooms; (ii) Preventive care with early identification of and response tohighrisk individuals and groups; and (iii) Chronic care management with early identification of chronicdiseases; (e) If its network of participating providers is insufficient tomeet the medical needs of enrollees, it contracts with outofnetworkmedical specialists, hospitals, and other facilities, including medicalcenters of excellence; (f) It has in place or is participating in, by a date specified bythe board and based on standards established by the health careauthority under this chapter, a comprehensive, shared, electronicpatient records and treatment tracking system and an electronicprovider payment system. The system shall comply with federal and SB 6221 p. 14 state confidentiality requirements, and enable providers to readilyobtain clinical information on inpatient and outpatient services,laboratory and radiological results, and other clinical data to improvequality and continuity of care; (g) It has a program to promote health care quality and increasethe transparency of health care cost and quality information; (h) It has adopted and implemented a strong policy to safeguardagainst conflicts of interest; and (i) It agrees to enroll and provide the benefits specified in thischapter to all partnership enrollees who choose the network, regardlessof the enrollee's age, sex, race, religion, national origin, sexualorientation, health status, marital status, disability status, oremployment status, except that a health care network may limit thenumber of new enrollees it accepts if the network certifies to theboard that accepting more than a specified number of enrollees wouldmake it impossible to provide all enrollees with the benefits specifiedin this chapter or maintain quality of care. (3) The board shall: (a) Review the bids submitted under this section and other evidenceprovided to the board demonstrating a particular bidder'squalifications. The board may make available to consumers quality andvalue scores for each plan; (b) Certify which networks are qualifying bidders; and (c) Classify the certified networks according to price and qualitymeasures after comparing their riskadjusted permonth bids andassessing their quality. The board shall classify the network thatbids the lowest price as the lowestcost benchmark network, and mayclassify as a lowcost benchmark network any network that has bid aprice that is close to the price bid by the lowestcost network, asdetermined by the board. The board shall classify any other network asa highercost network.

(1) The board shall provide an annual openenrollment period during which each enrollee may select a certifiedhealth care network from among those offered, or a feeforserviceoption. An enrollee who does not select a certified health carenetwork or the feeforservice option will be assigned randomly to oneof the lowestcost benchmark networks. If an enrollee enrolled in a p. 15 SB 6221highercost network fails to pay the additional payment for a highercost network, the board may reassign the enrollee to a benchmarknetwork. (2) The board: (a) Shall pay the network monthly for each enrolled enrollee. Theamount shall be the full riskadjusted permember permonth amount thatwas bid by the lowestcost network. The board may actuarially adjustthe payment for an enrollee based on age, sex, and other risk factorsdetermined by the board. In addition, enrollees in a higher-cost planshall monthly pay the network a premium as defined in section 11 ofthis act; (b) May retain a percentage of the dollar amounts established foreach enrollee to reimburse networks that have incurred disproportionaterisk not fully compensated for by the actuarial adjustment in theamount established for each eligible person. Any payment to acertified network under this subsection shall reflect thedisproportionate risk incurred by the network. (3)(a) The board shall establish payment rates to pay providers ofcovered services and articles under the feeforservice option, asdescribed under section 13 of this act. The payment rates must besufficient to ensure participation by high quality medicalpractitioners and promote participation by primary care providers. Theboard shall coordinate its feeforservice ratesetting efforts withthose of the department of social and health services, where suchcoordination would benefit access to services for both partnership andmedicaid enrollees. The board may adjust provider payments annually;such adjustments should restrain health care inflation while assuringcontinued access to a broad network of providers and quality services. (b) Except for deductibles, copayments, coinsurance, and any othercost sharing required or authorized under the plan, a provider ornetwork must accept as payment in full for a covered service or articlethe payment rate determined by the board and may not bill a enrolleewho receives the service or article any additional amount. (4) Except for prescription drugs to which a deductible applies,the board may assume the risk for, and pay directly for, lesscopayments, prescription drugs provided to all enrollees. Inimplementing this requirement, the board shall employ the services of SB 6221 p. 16 the prescription drug consortium, as defined under chapter 70.14 RCW,unless the board determines that another approach would be more costeffective, such as: (a) Joining another state's prescription drug purchasingarrangement to form a multistate purchasing group to negotiate withprescription drug manufacturers and distributors for reducedprescription drug prices; (b) Permitting a network or networks to maintain its own formulary;or (c) Contracting with a third party, such as a private pharmacybenefits manager, to negotiate with prescription drug manufacturers anddistributors for reduced prescription drug prices.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 74.09 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) By March 31, 2010, the department shall submit amendments tothe social security Title XIX state plan to expand the categoricallyneedy medicaid program effective January 1, 2010, to cover families andaged, blind, and disabled individuals up to two hundred percent of thefederal poverty level. To the degree possible, the eligible populationshall include enrollees in the basic health program. (2) The department, working with the board, as defined in section3 of this act, and consistent with the federal social security act,shall review payment rates under the state medical assistance programand may modify payment rates to more closely reflect those paid by theboard under the feeforservice option, as described under section 12of this act.

(1) In this chapter: (a) "Board" means the board of trustees of the Washington healthpartnership. (b) "Department" means the department of revenue. (c) "Dependent" means a spouse, an unmarried child under the age ofnineteen years, an unmarried child who is a fulltime student under theage of twentyfour years and who is financially dependent upon theparent, or an unmarried child of any age who is medically certified asdisabled and who is dependent upon the parent. p. 17 SB 6221 (d) "Eligible person" means a person who is eligible to participatein the plan, other than an employee or a selfemployed person. (e) "Employee" means a person who has an employer. (f) "Employer" means a person who is required under the internalrevenue code to file form 941. (g) "Medical inflation" means the percentage change between theUnited States consumer price index for all urban consumers, UnitedStates city average, for the medical care group only, including medicalcare commodities and medical care services, for the month of August ofthe previous year and the United States consumer price index for allurban consumers, United States city average, for the medical care grouponly, including medical care commodities and medical care services, forthe month of August 2007, as determined by the United States departmentof labor. (h) "Poverty line" means the federal poverty line, as defined under42 U.S.C. Sec. 9902(2), for a family the size of the individual'sfamily. (i) "Selfemployed individual" means an individual who is requiredunder the internal revenue code to file schedule SE. (j) "Social security wages" means: (i) The amount of wages, as defined in section 3121(a) of theinternal revenue code, paid to an employee by an employer in a taxableyear, up to a maximum amount that is equal to the social security wagebase; (ii) The amount of net earnings from selfemployment, as defined insection 1402(a) of the internal revenue code, received by an individualin a taxable year, up to a maximum amount that is equal to the socialsecurity wage base; and (iii) The amount of wages, as defined in section 3121(a) of theinternal revenue code, paid by an employer in a taxable year withrespect to employment, as defined in section 3121(b) of the internalrevenue code, up to a maximum amount that is equal to the socialsecurity wage base multiplied by the number of the employer'semployees.

(1) The board shall calculate the followingassessments for individuals, based on its anticipated revenue needs: SB 6221 p. 18 (a) For an employee who is under the age of sixtyfive, a percentof social security wages that is at least two percent and not more thanfour percent; and (b) For a selfemployed individual who is under the age of sixtyfive, a percent of social security wages that is at least nine percentand not more than ten percent. (2) The board shall calculate an assessment for employers, based onthe revenue required to fully fund the partnership. The assessmentshall be no less than nine percent and shall not exceed twelve percentof aggregate social security wages. (3) Beginning January 1, 2010, the department shall collect theindividual and employer assessment amounts that the board calculatesthrough a method devised by the department. The amounts collected bythe department shall be deposited into the Washington healthpartnership trust fund created under section 18 of this act. (4) The administrative and enforcement provisions in chapter 82.32RCW apply to this section.

There is established a separate, dedicatedtrust fund designated as the Washington health partnership trust fund,consisting of all amounts appropriated or transferred to or depositedin the fund, within the state treasury.

If any taxing district, as defined in RCW84.04.120, which reduces the costs of providing health care coverage tothe district's employees as a result of providing that coverage underthe Washington health partnership, as created by this act, togetherwith any supplemental coverage needed to ensure that the health carecoverage provided to employees of the taxing district is substantiallyactuarially equivalent to the coverage they received in 2008, thetaxing district shall distribute at least fifty percent of the savingsto the property taxpayers in the taxing district as a reduction in theproperty tax assessments. The reduction shall be calculated based onthe assessed value of the property and shall reduce the property taxesotherwise payable in that year.
Section 19 of this act applies to taxeslevied for collection in 2010 and thereafter.

The board and the partnership are entitledto the right of subrogation for reimbursement to the extent that anenrollee may recover reimbursement for health care services and itemsin an action or claim against any third party.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 43.370RCW to read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: The office of financial management strategic health planning shallcollaborate with the University of Washington center for healthworkforce studies, the department of health, and the higher educationcoordinating board, to develop a plan to increase the number andavailability of primary care providers in the state. By November 1,2009, the office shall submit a report to the legislature thatincludes: (1) Estimates of the number of primary care providers, includingtypes of providers by region, needed to provide the health careservices under this act for all state residents; and (2) Recommended actions to address identified shortages including,but not limited to: (a) Changes to reimbursement and fee structures under this act; (b) Changes to the loan forgiveness and conditional scholarshipprograms described in chapter 28B.115 RCW; and (c) Modifications to the higher education admission and educationalrequirements that would enhance the supply of primary care providers.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 74.38 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: By December 1, 2010, the board shall submit a report to thegovernor and the legislature regarding establishing a longterm careinsurance plan. The report shall include recommendations regarding theprovision of a guaranteed longterm care benefit to every Washingtonianincluding: SB 6221 p. 20 (1) Eligibility requirements including whether eligibilityrequirements should be the same as those used for the partnership, asdescribed under section 8 of this act; (2) Composition of a longterm care benefit package, includingskilled nursing and a communitybased service; (3) Length of time enrollees may receive benefits and the number ofepisodes of coverage; (4) Standards for longterm care services and providers offeringsuch services; and (5) Sources of revenue for the longterm care insurance plan,including the advisability of securing a federal waiver that wouldpermit continued use of medicaid funds for the purposes of longtermcare.

BillSection.RCWSLText: The insurance commissioner shall establish requirements in rule fora "network" as defined under section 3 of this act.
